justifications.decision: The object karmāṇi should not be translated as any and all activity in a secular sense. Śaṅkara identifies it as Agnihotra and other prescribed rites, and repeats that one who wishes to live should do precisely those śāstra-enjoined works.
options_considered: Vedic/śāstra-prescribed ritual works such as Agnihotra
justifications.chosen: karmāṇi = śāstra-prescribed ritual works, especially Agnihotra and the like; kurvan eva = only while doing them.

evidence.translation: “Therefore one should wish to live only while doing the works enjoined by scripture, Agnihotra and the like.”

justifications.decision: The optative jijīviṣet is glossed as ‘should wish to live,’ and samāḥ as ‘years.’ Śaṅkara adds that the wish to live a hundred years is a prāptānuvāda, a restatement of a natural fact; what is enjoined is ‘doing works alone.’ The translation therefore avoids making desire for longevity an independent Upaniṣadic duty.
options_considered: an injunction to desire long life as such
a restatement of the natural wish to live, with work-doing as the enjoined means
justifications.chosen: jijīviṣet śataṃ samāḥ = one should seek/wish to live a hundred years, but the real injunction is to do works while living.

evidence.translation: “jijīviṣet means ‘should wish to live’; śatam means ‘numbered by a hundred’; samāḥ means ‘years.’”},{

justifications.decision: The words evam, anyathā, and itaḥ are construed around prakāra: ‘in this manner,’ ‘a different manner,’ and ‘from this present manner.’ This rules out a merely spatial reading such as ‘not otherwise from here.’
justifications.chosen: evam … nānyathā itaḥ asti = in this manner there is no other way than this present mode of doing the prescribed works.

evidence.quote: evamevamprakāreṇa ... etasmādagnihotrādīni karmāṇi kurvato vartamānātprakārādanyathā prakārāntaraṃ nāsti
evidence.translation: “evam means ‘in this very manner’ ... apart from this present manner of doing Agnihotra and other works, there is no other different manner.”

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara construes tvayi with nare and supplies jijīviṣati and naramātrābhimānini. The translation therefore treats the second half as addressed to the person on the action-path, not to the renunciant knower described in the previous mantra.
options_considered: tvayi as a general ‘in you’ without qualification
tvayi nare as ‘in/for you, a man wishing to live and identifying as merely human’
justifications.chosen: tvayi and nare are locatives in apposition: ‘in/for you, as a man,’ specifically one wishing to live and identifying merely as a man.

evidence.translation: “in you, in a man wishing to live, [read from the unsegmented text as naramātrābhimānini itaḥ:] identifying merely as a man; from this ...”

justifications.decision: Although karma is morphologically the neuter nominative/accusative singular form in the mantra, Śaṅkara explains the intended sense as non-taint by karma and even specifies aśubha karma. Thus ‘does not cling/taint’ is preferable to a flat passive ‘karma is not smeared in the man.’
options_considered: karma as an inert subject: ‘karma is not smeared in a man’
idiomatic karmic non-taint: ‘action does not cling to/taint the man’
justifications.chosen: na karma lipyate nare = action does not cling to/taint the man; idiomatically, he is not tainted by karma.

evidence.quote: yena prakāreṇāśubhaṃ karma na lipyate karmaṇā na lipyata ityarthaḥ
evidence.translation: “by which manner evil karma does not cling; the meaning is, ‘he is not tainted by karma’ [lipyata is taken as the unproofread lipyate].”

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara explicitly frames mantra 1 as sannyāsin-jñānaniṣṭhā and mantra 2 as karmaniṣṭhā for the one incapable of that, insisting on the firm opposition between knowledge and action and on two distinct paths.
options_considered: universal endorsement of lifelong ritual action for all seekers
jñāna-karma-samuccaya, a combination of knowledge and action
a distinct action-path for the one not fit for renunciant knowledge
justifications.chosen: The mantra teaches karmaniṣṭhā for one unable to take the renunciant knowledge-path; it is not a doctrine of combining knowledge and ritual action.

evidence.quote: pūrveṇa saṃnyāsino jñānaniṣṭhoktā dvitīyena tadaśaktasya karmaniṣṭheti
evidence.translation: “By the previous [mantra] the knowledge-discipline of the renunciant was taught; by the second, the action-discipline of one incapable of that.”
“the opposition of knowledge and action, unshakable like a mountain.”

evidence.quote: imau dvāveva panthānāvanuniṣkrāntatarau bhavataḥ kriyāpathaścaiva purastātsaṃnyāsaścottareṇa
evidence.translation: “These two paths alone stand out: the path of ritual action first, and renunciation thereafter.”

translation:
Only doing here the ritual works (karmāṇi),
one should seek to live a hundred years.
Thus, for you—one who would live, taking yourself as just a man (nara)—
there is no other way than this:
action (karma) does not cling to the man.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might render karmāṇi as generic ‘actions’; Śaṅkara takes them as śāstra-prescribed rites such as Agnihotra.
It might make the desire to live a hundred years itself the injunction; Śaṅkara says this is prāptānuvāda and that ‘doing works alone’ is what is enjoined.
It might read itaḥ spatially as ‘from here’; the commentary glosses it modally as ‘from this manner/course.’
It might miss that tvayi nare is aimed at the person identifying as merely a man and wishing to live, not at the renunciant knowledge-seeker of mantra 1.
It might use this mantra to support a combination of knowledge and action; Śaṅkara explicitly rejects that by asserting their opposition and distinguishing the two paths.
It might translate na karma lipyate mechanically as ‘karma is not smeared in the man’; Śaṅkara gives the idiom ‘he is not tainted by karma.’
analyzer_disagreements: The analyzer’s local segmentation gives evā for eva; I read eva, supported by the commentary’s kurvanneva iha in line 1 and by the checked mūla sandhi eva+iha > eveha.
kurvan was tagged under root kṛ; for the required subanta analysis I record the participial nominal stem kurvant- (with weak stem kurvat-), while noting derivation from √kṛ.
jijīviṣet was tagged with lemma/stem jijīviṣ; for the required tinanta analysis I give the bare verbal root jīv and note the desiderative stem jijīviṣa-.
For tvayi, the analyzer does not specify gender; I supply masculine from the commentary’s apposition tvayi ... nare, while noting that the form is common to genders in isolation.
open_questions: Line 1 prints nivartayanneva; since the file is unproofread, this may stand for nirvartayanneva. I did not base a distinct ‘turning back’ interpretation on it, relying instead on the clear kurvanneva and karmāṇy agnihotrādīni glosses.
Line 4 prints lipyata in karmaṇā na lipyata ityarthaḥ; I treat this as unproofread for lipyate in the standard explanatory phrase karmaṇā na lipyate ity arthaḥ.
mula: kurvann eveha karmāṇi jijīviṣecchataṃ samāḥ | evaṃ tvayi nānyatheto 'sti na karma lipyate nare
commentary_lines: kurvanneva iha nivartayanneva karmāṇyagnihotrādīni jijīviṣejjīvitumicchecchataṃ śatasaṅkhyākāḥ samāḥ saṃvatsarān /
tathā ca prāptānuvādena yajjijīviṣecchataṃ varṣāṇi tat kurvanneva karmāṇītyetadvidhīyate /

evamevamprakāreṇa tvayi jijīviṣati nare naramātrābhimāninīta etasmādagnihotrādīni karmāṇi kurvato vartamānātprakārādanyathā prakārāntaraṃ nāsti yena prakāreṇāśubhaṃ karma na lipyate karmaṇā na lipyata ityarthaḥ /
kathaṃ punaridamavagamyate pūrveṇa saṃnyāsino jñānaniṣṭhoktā dvitīyena tadaśaktasya karmaniṣṭheti /
ucyateḥ jñānakarmaṇorvirodhaṃ parvatavadakampyaṃ yathoktaṃ na smarasi kim /
ihāpyuktaṃ 'yo hi jijīviṣet sa karma kurvan' 'īśāvāsyamidaṃ sarvam' 'tena tyaktena bhuñjīthāḥ' 'mā gṛdhaḥ kasyasviddhanam' iti ca /
'na jīvite maraṇe vā gṛdhiṃ kurvītāraṇyamiyāditi ca param ; tato na punariyāt' iti saṃnyāsāsanāt /
imau dvāveva panthānāvanuniṣkrāntatarau bhavataḥ kriyāpathaścaiva purastātsaṃnyāsaścottareṇa /
ityādi putrāya vicārya niścitamuktaṃ vyāsena vedācāryeṇa bhagavatā vibhāgañcānayoḥ darśayiṣyāmaḥ
